checks.about: Every board player is on their team's latest roster landing for the league's latest roster season: no retired, released or waived players.
checks.name: assert_board_rostered

checks.about: Every board row has played games behind its projection, season weights that with the replacement-level prior add up to one, a multiplier and a rest-of-season factor between 0 and 1, a games share between 0 and 1, and season and rest-of-season values no larger in magnitude than the values they scale.
checks.name: assert_board_values_sane

checks.about: Basketball arithmetic on every player-game that was played: PTS = 2*FGM + FG3M + FTM, FGM <= FGA, FG3M <= FGM, FG3A <= FGA, FTM <= FTA, REB = OREB + DREB.
checks.name: assert_box_arithmetic

checks.about: The player rows of a team-game add up to the team row for every counting stat except turnovers: the team total includes team turnovers (shot-clock and 8-second violations, inbound violations) that belong to no player, so turnovers are checked separately (warn_team_turnovers).
checks.name: assert_box_closure

checks.about: Every final regular-season or playoff game on the schedule that finished more than a day ago has a box score and play-by-play in gold. Preseason, All-Star, play-in and tournament finals are on the schedule but outside what the ingestors fetch (SPEC.md scope), so they are not counted as missing.
checks.name: assert_completeness

checks.about: In season, the latest game in gold is within 36 hours of the last completed scheduled game. Out of season (no completed scheduled game in the last 14 days) there is nothing to check.
checks.name: assert_freshness_in_season

checks.about: The chaos switch: `--vars '{chaos: true}'` makes this error-severity check fail on purpose, so the publish gate and the incident path can be exercised end to end on demand.
checks.name: chaos_deliberate_failure

checks.about: At least 99% of a season's played player-games are matched to ESPN through the crosswalk (SPEC.md phase 4). The league lists inactive players with a line of zeros that ESPN does not carry, so the rate is judged over players who were on the floor. Seasons with fewer than 100 played player-games are too small to judge.
checks.name: warn_crosswalk_coverage

checks.about: Made field goals in play-by-play per player-game equal FGM in the box score.
checks.name: warn_event_box_agreement

checks.about: Lines inside plausible bounds for professional basketball: totals between 100 and 300 points, spreads under 40, both sides implied to score, and the two implied scores adding up to the total.
checks.name: warn_game_line_sanity

checks.about: The latest run per source and league landed a payload count within 3 MAD of the median of the trailing 14 runs (only once there are at least 5 earlier runs to compare with). Full-refresh and backfill runs (explicit windows longer than 10 days) are left out.
checks.name: warn_ingest_volume_anomaly

checks.about: At least 80% of the players on the latest injury report are linked to a league player id; the rest are usually players on two-way or developmental deals missing from both rosters.
checks.name: warn_injury_links

checks.about: At least 90% of a season's actions have five players a side on the floor. Period starters after the first period are inferred, so a player who plays a whole period without an action or a substitution is missed; a drop below 90% means the substitution format changed.
checks.name: warn_lineup_completeness

checks.about: Player minutes per team-game add up to the team minutes (200 WNBA / 240 NBA, +25 per overtime) within one minute.
checks.name: warn_minutes_closure

checks.about: Players on the league's newest injury report, for upcoming games, that could not be linked to a league player id (by name within the team). A few two-way or newly signed players are expected; more means a team name or a name form the link does not handle.
checks.name: warn_official_injury_links

checks.about: Court coordinates inside the half court (tenths of a foot from the basket) and the three-point flag consistent with distance: a three is at least 21 feet out, a two at most 24.
checks.name: warn_shot_location_sanity

checks.about: Team turnovers are the players' turnovers plus team turnovers (no player charged), so the team figure must be at least the players' sum and rarely more than a handful above it.
checks.name: warn_team_turnovers

checks.about: Arena cities in the schedule that the venues seed cannot place: their games get no travel or altitude context until the city is added to seeds/venues.csv.
checks.name: warn_venue_cities

models.description: The five players on the floor for each side at every play-by-play action (substitution intervals; period starters inferred after the first period).
models.name: event_lineups
notes: The five players on the floor for each team at every play-by-play action.

The league's play-by-play names only the player leaving on a substitution ("SUB: Key FOR Fagbenle", with the leaving player's id); the player coming on is matched by surname to the game's box score for that team. When two teammates share a surname the feed adds the start of the given name ("SUB: K. Mitchell FOR T. Mitchell", "SUB: Jay. Williams FOR Mitchell"), which must match the given name too; names the feed writes in the other order ("Xu" for Han Xu) match by given name, and a name with more words ("J.J. Redick") by its last word. A player's time on the floor is a set of intervals within a period: a period starter is on from the start, a substitution in opens an interval and one out closes it; the action that is the substitution belongs to the lineup before it. Order is the game clock within the period, with the action number only breaking ties: the feed logs some substitutions late, so action numbers alone are not chronological.

Period starters: period 1 from the box score (starters carry a position). Later periods are inferred: a player is on at the start of a period when, in that period, their first substitution is out, or they record an action before any substitution in. A player who plays a whole period without an action or a substitution is not seen; lineup_complete (five a side) is false for those actions, and the share of complete lineups is checked per season.

notes: One row per game: home and away sides folded from the team game log.

The game log marks a side as home when its matchup reads "vs." and away when it reads "@". At a neutral site (league showcase games abroad, a cup final) both teams read "vs.", so the sides are ranked per game, home first, then by team id: the two rows always fold into one game, and the home side of a neutral-site game is the lower team id, flagged by `neutral_site`.

models.description: The board: value above replacement per rostered player from the projected line, recent form, the per-game line, injury status and rest-of-season scaling.
models.name: mart_board
notes: The draft and in-season board: one row per rostered player per league.

Value is scored once, on each player's projected per-game line (mart_player_projection: per-minute production times projected minutes), in two passes. Pass one standardises the nine categories over the pool_size players with the most projected minutes; pass two repeats it over the pool_size players pass one values most, so the means and spreads describe the players a fantasy league actually rosters. Counting categories are z-scores of the projected per-game numbers (turnovers negative); percentages are volume-weighted, (player pct - pool pct) x attempts per game, standardised over the pool.

Every category then has replacement level subtracted: the average category score of the next `teams` players after the pool. Zero is a freely available player, so the nine values sum to value per game above replacement (value_per_game) and a punt build is the sum without the punted columns. value_total counts games: value per game times the projected share of team games the player plays (games_share), since a missed game is filled by a replacement-level player; a value below replacement is left as it is.

Alongside the value the row carries the current season's z-scores over the whole season and the last twenty and ten games, the per-game line, the projected line itself, and the player's age and rookie status from the roster, so the app can rank on recent form or raw production too and filter the way a fantasy manager does.

Rest of season counts regular-season games only, the games fantasy leagues score. While some remain, ros_factor is the team's remaining share of its regular season times the availability multiplier, the share of those games the player is expected to play given the current injury report (out: the games before the expected return, or all of them without a date; doubtful 0.75 of a game, questionable 0.5, day-to-day 0.25). value_rest_of_season scales value above replacement by it; a value below replacement is left as it is, since a missing game from a player not worth rostering costs nothing. Once the regular season is over (playoffs or the off-season) season_complete is true and ros_factor is 1. games_next_7 counts playoff games too.

The pool is the top 180 NBA or top 90 WNBA players by total minutes in the window; means and standard deviations come from the pool only. Counting categories use per-game averages. Percentages use a volume-weighted impact: (player pct - pool pct) x player attempts per game, standardised over the pool. Turnovers count negative.

models.description: One projected per-game line per player on a current roster: the current season and the two before, weighted by games and recency, starting from a replacement-level line.
models.name: mart_player_projection
notes: One projected line per player on a current roster: what the board scores.
The projection separates how much a player plays from what they do while playing:

- Minutes per game: each season's minutes per game counted by games played times a minutes recency weight (per league, var fantasy.<league>.minutes_recency), so a change of role in the current season shows within a few games where the league's roles move a lot (WNBA). A past season spent mostly on another team counts for var fantasy_team_change (0.25) of its minutes weight: the role was a different team's. Per-minute production carries over.

- Production per minute: each season's totals over its minutes, counted by minutes played times the production recency weight (var fantasy_recency: 1.0, 0.25, 0.08). A season of 60 games at 8 minutes counts for far less than 60 games at 34.
- Per-game line: production per minute times projected minutes.

- Games share (durability): the share of their team's regular-season games a player played in the seasons they appeared in, by the same recency, regressed toward a typical share by durability_games games (var fantasy.<league>.durability_games, fantasy_durability). Regular season only: playoff games would make every team that missed the playoffs look as if its players sat out.

Every projection also starts from prior_games games of a replacement-level player (var fantasy: 3 NBA, 5 WNBA), at that player's minutes and per-minute production, so a short sample moves a projection only part of the way and a missing season adds nothing. All settings were chosen by backtest (ADR 0003).

The replacement-level line is the average line of the players just outside a fantasy league's rosters by total minutes (ranks pool_size + 1 to pool_size + teams) in the league's latest complete regular season.

Current roster: the player is on their team's latest roster landing for the league's latest roster season. A player waived or released drops off with the next landing, and a retired player is on no roster at all, so neither is projected. Only players with at least one game in the three seasons are projected.

Each side of a game carries a matchup value: how much a player's value per game moves with the opponent's defence and the game's expected pace, from replaying past seasons (ADR 0003: one standard deviation of opponent defence is worth about 0.2 value per game in the NBA, against a game-to-game swing of about 2.5; var fantasy_matchup). A team's defensive rating and pace blend this season to date with last season, last season counting as prior_games games, so early in a season (and for a reworked roster) the current games take over as they accumulate; early on, last season's team defence was the better guide. Ratings are standardised over the league's teams. A player's past results against an opponent predicted nothing (correlation 0.00 to 0.04) and are not used.

Each game also carries its betting line where the sportsbooks have posted one (silver game_lines): the home spread, the over/under, and the points each side is implied to score. The line is shown alongside the matchup value and does not change it until a backtest says it adds to it.

models.name: mart_streamers
notes: Streaming candidates: one row per player active in the league's current season, with the team's games over the next seven days, the minutes trend and recent production.
Active means at least three games this season and a game within the last thirty days of the league's season so far, so players from earlier seasons never appear.

The trends compare recent games with a baseline: minutes over the last five games, value over the last ten. The baseline is the player's games this season before the window, blended with the player's latest earlier season (last season, or the one before for a player who missed it) counted as up to 10 games. Early in a season the window is the whole season, so the baseline is last season; late in a season it is mostly this one. A player with neither (a rookie's first games) has no trend rather than a misleading zero.

Each row also carries the last-ten-games z-score per category, for ranking by the categories a manager needs, and the player's board rank and value, for leaving out players a league of a given size has most likely rostered (null for a player not on a current roster). The value baseline uses the season z-score, which includes the window; with few games before the window it is weighted toward last season accordingly. While the league is between seasons the same columns describe who finished the season strongly, and season_complete says so.
